title: Marva Josie and doing what feels comfortable
summary: Humes says Marva Josie would be better singing as she wants, not as a glamour girl. She herself never thinks about what others are doing and could sing rock if she wanted.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah sure that's the business, isn't it? Well listen, there are some gals that have quite alot on the ball and somehow or another can't make it. What about Marva Josie? I mean it's a shame. The Girl tries hard. She's a pretty girl. She's got a
pretty voice. But somehow or other nothing happens.
Well, I think if she would go and sing like she wanted to sing and not like Earl wants to make a glamour girl out of her, well I think she'd be much better off.
Yeah. I mean because she can sing. Like "Poor Butterfly". She can sing.

And the thing is, you know, a cross between two schools because she looks at the rock singers and thinks they're making alot of money. And she knows they're not doing a good job. So she thinks to herself, why can't she move in on that. But you know . . .

I don't know. Maybe that's where I make my mistakes. You know, I don't ever think about what everybody else is doing. I just do what I want to do and what I feel comfortable doing, and I hope you like it.
Right. Well that's the whole thing.
And I just try to get through to everybody. I can sing rock if I wanted to.
Yes, I guess you can. No, but see you don't have the problem because God gave you a gift.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
He gave you a gift and your personality and your gift go together, and this is what you forget. This is you.
